text: Are we ready? Okay. Good afternoon, everyone. Um, thank you for being here today. I call to order this February eighteenth, twenty twenty-six school board retreat. Um, in terms of our plans for today, uh, my hope is that we will be able to ground ourselves through this conversation.

Dr. Rasheed? Thank you, Chair Chandler. Um, I think this is a great opportunity, I guess, to

kinda open the floor for a discussion. Thank you, Madam Chair. and that, that should be where we are focused. Thank you, Miss Labelle. Mr. Pepper? So... And, uh, thank you, Madam Chair. Um, and to approach every conversation we have,

whether one-on-one or as a whole board, with both kind of where we're coming from, but also respecting that everyone has their own background, their own experiences, their own difference of opinion. Um, I think that's very important. Thank you. Um, Miss Chernov? Thank you, Madam Chair. Um, I'm looking forward to this more of a day of listening and just hearing where people are at on the various topics.

Um, it goes without saying that students are at the center, I think, but, um, sure, I'll reiterate that.... And additionally,

I, um, hope that we can figure out what the best way to communicate is, because I think in terms of a board that starts to wander off the path, is a board that's not communicating, and a board that, um, operates in more of a blind side environment, than making sure that everyone is read in on what, what's important and what's coming up, and, and kind of knowing where we stand. I realize our quorum rules make that challenging at times, um, but I think that that was something in the last two years that we really were

striving for, and so I'm hoping to reestablish that foundation today. Thank you. Vice Chair Donahue? Thank you, Madam Chair. Uh, I echo, um, the sentiments of my colleagues, and only wanted to kind of add to/reinforce, um, you know, after two years on the board, I have

been, I have been pleasantly surprised by the working relationships that I've been able to, to forge doing this work, um, and with, with people who I disagree with, um, on sometimes on policy issues, sometimes on what I view as moral ethical issues, and as well as on political

issues. Uh, because as many people have already pointed out, we are here to do what is in the best interest of the students and staff of Loudoun County. And I have, like I said, been pleasantly surprised that when we are able to focus on that and to give each other the space to hear each other out and assume good intentions on the part of our colleagues, and have open

listening ears and try to reach compromises, um, it's gone in many ways better than I, than I thought it would. Uh, and so I look forward to continuing to work on that myself, um, with with the new board members, uh, and, uh, as well as with, uh, all of our returning board members as well, to continue to work together to prioritize the best interests of Loudoun

County. Thank you. Any further comments? All right. Well, um, as part of this, uh, table setting exercise, I thought it would be important for us to look at some of our foundational documents, and to that extent, I have asked, um, staff to sort of speak just briefly to an overview, and, and then I hope that we can have a conversation for how we intend, um, to work

together. Um, so with that, we'll move on, um, to item three point zero one, our board norms and policy review, and, uh, Mr. Allen will kick us off. Thank you, Chair Chandler. Policy ten thirty-five, entitled School Board Norms, Protocols, and Violation, was adopted in April twenty twenty-one. It sets forth the general norms for school board members to include social media norms, protocols to include expectations for how to respond to various communications or

requests from parents and guardians, and the media, communications with one another, committee chair reports, visiting schools, professional development, and then lastly, sets forth the processes and procedures for addressing when school board members are alleged to have violated any of the norms or protocols, school board policies, LCPS regulations, or law. The LAMP committee reviewed this policy last fall, and it's my understanding that at its December ninth,

twenty twenty-five meeting, the committee voted to move this policy out of the committee to the full school board, so that it could be taken up with the board as an information item, with the caveat or request that the school board chair hold the item in December, so that it could be discussed in a work session after the new school board was seated and a new s- chair is elected. So this is the first opportunity to do that. My understanding is that the idea of presenting this item today is for the

school board to have a dialogue about its norms and protocols as they currently exist in policy ten thirty-five, and to determine if there are other expectations, norms, protocols, that the school board has an interest in memorializing in this policy. One item that Ms. Chernoff raised during her tenure on the LAMP committee was whether the board has an interest to memorialize the duties and roles of board leadership, either in policy ten thirty-five or in a separate,

distinct policy. In response to such requests, staff incorporated, um, the red lines that you'll see, um, and on lines one twenty-nine to four thirty-two, which are about seven pages or so. These are compiled from other policies and governing documents to include the annual resolution, um, annual organizational resolution. Additionally, you'll see red lines, um, for section B, professional development, on lines seventy-eight to eighty-eight, which

incorporates language from policy twenty-one forty, um, which is orientation and professional development for new school board members, as that policy was recently revised by the school board, as some of you will recall, on December sixteenth, twenty twenty-five, to focus solely on the orientation and professional development for new school board members, rather than including continuing professional developments as required under Virginia law. Reviewing this with fresh eyes, that language preexists in policy

ten thirty-five, um, albeit in a paraphrased form, in lines four ninety-one to four ninety-seven, which is under section E8, protocols. I'm happy to kick this off since a lot of these changes were at my request, and then with the approval of the LA and P committee, which I very much appreciated. So learning the policies and the structures that we have, especially as it relates to what the best practices across the state or in our neighboring districts, was, was something that kept coming up frequently.

And one of the things that would come up is, you know, in other policies, as listed here, there was lots of responsibilities of the board chair, it seemed to me, that were being mentioned sporadically throughout. It turned out to be more extensive than I even anticipated, um, having all of those roles and responsibilities in one place just so that

we could see them. So I'm appreciative of that. I don't know-- I would- I really don't have a personal preference on whether we create another policy out of this one. This makes it quite lengthy, but I do like having it all in one place. I think it, it provides transparency for the community, for the board. If you're a new board member, you know what that role would be and what, what the expectations are. Also, if you are not the chair, there is a lot here about how school board members interface with the chair, and so I think that that's

important to know in terms of accountability as well. So I would like for us to stick with having them all in one place, um, but the form of that, I'm-- I don't really have a preference. Um, as I was reading through it again this weekend, uh, one of the things that I, I mentioned in committee and I feel like still is lacking here in terms of the duties, is what is the communication expectations back to the board, and when is the board solicited for, I guess,

consensus feedback would be the best way to say it. Um, we talk a lot in this board about the will of the board, and of course, that remains true for a majority. How are those opinions solicited throughout these various processes? I think a blanket statement about how communication is expected and, and turned around would be helpful. It is something I feel that is missing. Thank you.

Ms. Ricardi? Thank you so much. So, um, I also went through this, kind of, and took my time reading through it this weekend, and I think it was really helpful to see everything in one place. of the organization as a whole. But I feel like there's an enormous, uh, number of things

in here that I'm uncomfortable with, and I, I look at this through kind of a, a, kind of the both sides of the coin thing. I get, um, why some of these things are probably in here. It makes... Some of it, I, I get the gist of it. Um, I think I would like to see this be a much more collaborative, um,

scenario, and in that, our, you know, uh-- and this isn't you specifically, but just as a function of the board chair role and the vice chair role, that, um, we as a board are read in on, on everything. tightened up. Um, and that'd be an interesting conversation. policy, um, having some conversations around the, um, actual items, and then having it come before the full board. And, and having our conversation, um, I-- and I, I will say, I really have appreciated having this all together in one

place. It-- I could find it, uh, very difficult to have to try and go and find in every policy, um, where all of these things lie. Thank you, Madam Chair. Just to follow up on some of Ms. Ricardi's comments, I-- It, it is

So for me- ... it's not a matter-- I mean, we elect the chair, and, you know, that's part of this role, and the vice chair, although the vice chair's roles are

specifically between the superintendent or the chair or legal counsel, that we are constantly... So I think having that accountability in the policy would help me. The individual items, having been through this

process, feel appropriate to me in terms of the level of getting the work done in a division this size. Thank you, Ms. Chernov. Um, Vice Chair Donahue? Thank you, Madam Chair.
